authority.peoplePolicy: People in catalogue references inform scale, use, supervision, spectator and circulation logic only. No people belong in deterministic park geometry or skins.

validatedRules: Fit complete standard modules; repeat them when capacity and parcel geometry allow, never stretch a court or field.
Treat the archetype's spatial topology as a family contract: shared compounds, podded layouts, loops, treatment trains, terraces, rows and habitat mosaics are not interchangeable.
Place entrances, gates, spectator or caregiver edges, service access and accessible routes before decorative planting.
Assign residual land an intentional archetype role such as meadow, rain garden, orchard, social terrace, habitat buffer or retained canopy.
Render a family-specific object kit and deterministic equipment count, not generic tree and bench scatter alone.
Use reference-derived multi-material surfaces with wear, joints, soil, mulch, sand, water, meadow and planting transitions instead of monochrome fills.
Keep large buildings separate; park recipes reserve pads, forecourts and access clearances only.

providerWarnings.warning: One image invented a basketball court and a person. Reject unrelated program creep and all generated people.
The providers produced overly intertwined multi-loop layouts. Enforce one closed primary circuit with bounded skill and bypass branches.
Provider court counts diverged. The selected variant and deterministic fit solver own the number of standard court modules.
Aerial imagery did not reliably expose a safe nine-hole sequence. Tee, basket, fairway and crossing validation must remain graph-based.
Both providers drifted toward generic formal quadrangles. Preserve the chosen courtyard variant's exact building-edge clearances, canopy, screen and study-zone identity.

strengths: All 130 parent archetypes and 520 variants resolve to LEGO family, appearance-kit and planting identities.
Basketball already uses fitted guide geometry and exact one-hoop versus two-hoop placements; an oversized parcel repeats complete courts rather than stretching one.
Sixteen reviewed kit manifests provide 70 GLBs for basketball, skate, dog, inclusive play, splash, community garden, nature play, pump track, calisthenics and major regulation-sports anchors.
Reference-derived PBR skins, tile-flattening bases and one-park-at-a-time generation are already established.
gaps: The general scatter layer still exposes only tree, bench, playground and pavilion roles; exact guide-anchored program placement is currently implemented most completely for basketball hoops.
Several live City Prompt trials remain visually sparse compared with both catalogue references and the new API studies, especially ecological, courtyard and late-catalogue families.
Many late variants share parent geometry and procedural props while relying on their skins for identity; they need variant-owned secondary object sets and placement rules.
Senior fitness and woodland memorial variants inherit object kits aimed at calisthenics and classical memorials rather than their own specialized equipment and quiet-use character.
